chunks: From him, from Ayyūb, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Saʿd ibn Abī Khalaf, who said:

ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn asked Abā al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام about a house belonging to a man in a town, or an estate, by which he passes. He said: If it is among what he had already lived in, he should perform the salat there in full; and if it is among what he had not lived in, then he should shorten.

key_terms.الدَّارِ: a house or residence owned by a person
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: the prescribed salat whose form depends here on residence or travel status
key_terms.سَكَنَهُ: lived in it or resided there
key_terms.فَلْيُقَصِّرْ: let him shorten the salat as a traveler

ai.seo_question: When does a traveler pray in full at his own property or estate?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the traveler who passes by a house or estate that belongs to him. If it is a place in which he had previously resided, he performs the salat there in full; if he had not resided in it, he shortens the salat as a traveler.
